blocker.summary: r467 made two failed live-gdb attempts to catch the movie-worker's KeWaitForMultipleObjects state at the stall point (a conditional breakpoint that never fired in 12+ minutes due to per-call evaluation cost; a direct gdb launch that hit a debugger-specific SIGSEGV in rex_sub_821E4378 never seen outside gdb, plus a harness time-budget kill), then found a more important correction via a THIRD launch that avoided gdb entirely: running ac6recomp directly on the same Xvfb display shows the exact same KeSetEvent(ptr=82916E3C) -> KeWaitForMultipleObjects(objects=[82916E2C 82916E08]) result=0 pattern r466 read as the stall symptom occurring from the FIRST SECOND after boot (00:44:50, before any world/cinematic loading). This corrects r466: the loop is not stall-specific, it runs continuously from process start, which looks like normal per-tick polling rather than a genuinely stuck thread. The real root cause of the world/campaign-transition stall is still NOT established, but the 'movie-worker is stuck' theory is now weakened by this evidence -- the actual blocker is likely elsewhere. All spawned processes (ac6recomp/gdb/Xvfb) and scratch directories were cleaned up; the native profile was not touched this cycle (no rebuild). Named for r468: look at what governs the [ac6-visual-phase] world=1 activation itself rather than this specific wait site; a Ghidra headless pass on the ac6-us project for that activation's static xrefs may be more productive than another long gdb attach. Still open, non-blocking: (1) the pinned shader registry coverage gap (r456) remains the main track once this is resolved; (2) once PinnedShaderRuntime wiring is judged mature, reconsider the native backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438/r454-r462); (3) update tools/prepare.py/build.py to default to the current ISO path (r452/r453, convenience only).
